solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Brightly-coloured bird with a flower from the east

indicators.note: in an across clue, coming from the east means reading from right to left

parts.note: W is the standard abbreviation for with
taken as written
a flower is something that flows, a river; the Cam flows through Cambridge

explanation.surface: A birdwatcher spots a vivid bird carrying a bloom it fetched from the east.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flower' tempts you towards blooms, but in crosswords it is often a river.
explanation.definitionFit: The macaw is a large tropical parrot famous for its vivid plumage.

clue.text: Serviceman digesting puff and spiced liquid

indicators.note: something digesting takes food inside it, so one word swallows the other

parts.note: a marine is a soldier serving at sea
a puff is a piece of promotional praise, an advert

explanation.surface: A soldier is wolfing down a pastry and some spicy sauce.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Puff' looks like pastry but means a promotional plug.
explanation.definitionFit: A marinade is a seasoned liquid in which meat or fish is soaked before cooking.

clue.text: Church painter, a nineteenth century reformer

parts.note: CH is the usual abbreviation for church
a painter is an artist

explanation.surface: A painter of church interiors who was also a Victorian campaigner.
explanation.walkthrough: The Chartists were a British working-class movement of the 1830s-40s demanding votes for all men.
explanation.definitionFit: Chartists campaigned for the People's Charter, a programme of electoral reform in Victorian Britain.

clue.text: Working in cafe, failed to remember about party and play

parts.note: working in a cafe is waiting at tables

indicators.note: about means going round, so one word surrounds the other

parts.note: failed to remember means forgot
a do is a party

explanation.surface: A cafe worker forgot about a party and a play.
explanation.walkthrough: The party goes between the O and T of the forgetting word.
explanation.definitionFit: Waiting for Godot is Samuel Beckett's celebrated absurdist stage drama.

clue.text: Formidable family keeping a large old female cat

indicators.note: keeping means holding inside, so one word goes within the others

parts.note: formidable, forbidding: grim
taken as written
L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large
one's family is one's kin

explanation.surface: A fearsome family looks after a big elderly she-cat.
explanation.walkthrough: The family holds A and L between the formidable word and itself.
explanation.definitionFit: A grimalkin is an archaic word for a cat, especially an old she-cat, as in Macbeth's witches.

clue.text: Eg Scottish Celt in strong wind, we hear

indicators.note: we hear signals a word that is spoken like another but spelt differently

parts.note: a strong wind is a gale

explanation.surface: A Highlander caught out in a storm.
explanation.definitionFit: A Gael is a Gaelic-speaking Celt from Scotland, Ireland or the Isle of Man.

clue.text: On which to play casually, visiting home and part of hospital?

definitions.text: On which to play casually, visiting home and part of hospital?

indicators.note: a visitor goes inside a place, so one word sits within another

parts.note: being at home is being in
to strum is to play a guitar idly
ENT is the ear, nose and throat department

explanation.surface: A patient strumming a guitar on a hospital ward.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition: something you strum, perhaps at home or on a ward.
explanation.definitionFit: A musical instrument is what one plays, casually or otherwise.

clue.text: An Athenian man briefly heading state, holding republican views

parts.note: taken as written
Timon of Athens is Shakespeare's misanthropic Athenian
the prefix archi- means chief or leading, and sits at the head of a word
Cal is a short form of California
signals that the state further on appears in shortened form

explanation.surface: An Athenian briefly leading a state while holding republican opinions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Briefly' points to the shortened form of the US state; 'heading' gives the prefix meaning chief, as in archiepiscopal.
explanation.definitionFit: Being opposed to monarchy is the stance of a republican.

clue.text: Pellets livestock ultimately pick at? Not the first

indicators.note: not the first means the opening letter is swapped out for another
'ultimately' keeps only the last letter of 'livestock'

parts.note: the final letter of livestock
to pick at is to nibble, here without its first letter

explanation.surface: Do farm animals peck at their feed pellets? Not first in line, anyway.
explanation.walkthrough: The opening N of nibble is replaced by the K at the end of livestock.
explanation.definitionFit: Kibble is coarsely ground meal formed into pellets, used as pet or animal food.

clue.text: Legal official's polite refusal on track

parts.note: no, ta is a polite way of declining
RY is the abbreviation for railway, a track

explanation.surface: A lawyer politely says no while standing on a railway line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ta' is British slang for thank you.
explanation.definitionFit: A notary is a public officer who certifies documents and witnesses signatures.

clue.text: Inclination to study Italian at first with head

parts.note: to read is to study, as at university

indicators.note: at first asks for only the opening letter of the word before it

parts.note: the opening letter of Italian
a ness is a headland, as in Loch Ness or Sheerness

explanation.surface: A student keen to read Italian, starting with the head.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Head' is a promontory here, not a part of the body.
explanation.definitionFit: Readiness is a willingness or disposition to do something.

clue.text: Asian country's temperature, the writer hazards

parts.note: T is the abbreviation for temperature
the writer is I, the setter; hazards means bets, so I bet

explanation.surface: A traveller guesses at the climate of a Himalayan land.
explanation.definitionFit: Tibet is a Himalayan region, historically an independent Asian nation, now governed by China.

clue.text: Wally returning container with end broken off

indicators.note: breaking the end off a word loses its final letter
returning means going back, so the word is read from right to left

parts.note: a tin is a container
with, minus its last letter

explanation.surface: Someone bringing back a jar whose rim has snapped off.
explanation.walkthrough: A wally is British slang for a silly person.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words mean a foolish, stupid person.

clue.text: Soldiers (male) bitten by sort of bear's tooth

indicators.note: being bitten by something means being held between its jaws, inside it

parts.note: the polar bear is one kind of bear
RE is the Royal Engineers
M is the abbreviation for male

explanation.surface: Male soldiers bitten by a fierce bear.
explanation.walkthrough: The soldiers and the male go together inside the bear's type.
explanation.definitionFit: A premolar is one of the teeth between the canines and the molars.

clue.text: Group of states in defeat or in disarray

indicators.note: in disarray means thrown into disorder, so the letters are muddled

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: An alliance of nations in defeat or in chaos.
explanation.definitionFit: A federation is a union of self-governing states under a central government.

clue.text: Clash involving Times grandee

indicators.note: involving here means making involved, tangled and complicated, so the letters get twisted

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A row breaks out involving a bigwig at The Times newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Involving' reads as 'concerning', but it is the shuffle signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A clash is a quarrel or conflict of opinion, a disagreement.

clue.text: Revolutionary stunt ruined old joke

indicators.note: ruined means wrecked, so the letters are broken up and rearranged

parts.note: Che Guevara is the crossword's stock revolutionary
the letters of stunt rearranged

explanation.surface: A rebel's ruined stunt becomes a worn-out gag.
explanation.definitionFit: A chestnut is a stale, much-repeated joke or story.

clue.text: Impulse to place in box part of transmission

indicators.note: placing one thing in another puts it inside

parts.note: to box is to spar, with sparring split around the insert
an impulse is an urge
the end of spar

explanation.surface: An urge to put something in a gearbox.
explanation.walkthrough: Box is a verb: to spar.
explanation.definitionFit: A spur gear is a toothed wheel with straight teeth, a component of mechanical transmissions.

clue.text: Speed regulator's joint position of authority in US state

definitions.text: position of authority in US state

parts.note: a governor is a device that limits an engine's speed
the hip is a joint

explanation.surface: An engine's speed limiter joins in a role of state power.
explanation.definitionFit: A governorship is the office of governor, the elected head of an American state.

clue.text: Peg installed in standard type of harpsichord

indicators.note: something installed in another thing goes inside it

parts.note: standard, fixed: set
a peg is a pin

explanation.surface: A tuning peg fitted in a harpsichord of standard design.
explanation.walkthrough: The pin goes between the S and the ET.
explanation.definitionFit: A spinet is a small harpsichord with the strings set at an angle to the keyboard.

clue.text: Cower endlessly round back of bothy, showing distress

indicators.note: round means surrounding, so one piece goes inside another
endlessly means without its final letter

parts.note: to cower is to cringe

indicators.note: the back of a word is its final letter

parts.note: the last letter of bothy

explanation.surface: Someone cowering in a remote hut, visibly upset.
explanation.walkthrough: A bothy is a Scottish hillside shelter hut.
explanation.definitionFit: Crying, shedding tears, is a sign of distress.

clue.text: Ancient countryman praying desperately outside hospital

indicators.note: acting desperately means wildly and out of order, so the letters are scrambled
outside means wrapping round something else

parts.note: the letters of praying rearranged
H is the hospital sign

explanation.surface: An old rustic praying hard outside the hospital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Countryman' means a native of a country, not someone rural.
explanation.definitionFit: A Phrygian was a native of Phrygia, an ancient kingdom of Asia Minor.

clue.text: Follow-up drink for one making an impression

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a drink taken after another, such as beer after a spirit
second meaning: an engraver who embosses or chases metal

explanation.surface: Buying another round to impress someone.
explanation.definitionFit: A chaser is a drink following another, and also a metalworker who chases, embossing designs into metal.

clue.text: Woman from north involved in Muslim festival

indicators.note: being involved in something means being inside it

parts.note: Eid is a Muslim festival, split around the insert
N is the abbreviation for north
the end of Eid

explanation.surface: A northern woman taking part in an Islamic celebration.
explanation.definitionFit: Enid is a woman's first name, crossword shorthand for a woman.

clue.text: Minor divinity reported near a pond at last

indicators.note: reported means said out loud, so the sound counts and not the spelling

parts.note: near a, as spoken in a non-rhotic accent

indicators.note: at last asks for the final letter only

parts.note: the last letter of pond

explanation.surface: A lesser god is said to be lurking near a pond.
explanation.definitionFit: A naiad is a water nymph of Greek myth, a minor deity of springs and rivers.

clue.text: Blamelessness of civil engineer visiting pub in the past

indicators.note: a visitor goes inside a place, so one piece sits within another

parts.note: an inn is a pub
once, opened up to take the insert
CE is the abbreviation for civil engineer
the rest of once

explanation.surface: An engineer claims he was innocent of being at the pub that night.
explanation.walkthrough: The engineer sits inside the 'once' that follows the pub.
explanation.definitionFit: Innocence is freedom from guilt, the state of being blameless.

clue.text: Tipsy English chap screwed up, perhaps?

parts.note: tight is slang for drunk
E is the abbreviation for English
Ned is a man's name, a chap

explanation.surface: A drunk Englishman has made a mess of things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Screwed up' reads as botched, but means turned like a screw, an example of tightening, hence 'perhaps'.
explanation.definitionFit: Something screwed up is made fast by turning, one way of being tightened.

clue.text: More recent part of school at Erith

indicators.note: part of says the answer is a portion of the words that follow

parts.note: letters running across the word boundary

explanation.surface: A newer section of a school in Erith.
explanation.walkthrough: Erith is a town in south-east London.
explanation.definitionFit: Later means coming afterwards in time, so more recent.
